summary: Join our Climate Change Mitigation in Oil and Gas course to discover innovative solutions for reducing emissions and promoting sustainability in the industry.
lede: Climate change mitigation in oil and gas helps you build a credible emissions baseline, identify major sources, and prioritize methane reduction, flaring control, and energy-efficiency measures. You will work with carbon accounting, the GHG Protocol, IPCC Guidelines, ISO 14064-1, and practical emissions registers to support verifiable reporting and sound operational decisions. Through hands-on exercises, you will screen abatement options, develop a mitigation roadmap, and turn operational findings into a board-ready summary. The course also introduces lifecycle thinking, science-based target setting, carbon pricing concepts, and digital monitoring approaches while accounting for data gaps, legacy assets, capital limits, contractor dependencies, and competing production targets.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who need to reduce emissions, justify mitigation investments, and produce credible climate reporting across oil and gas operations.
prerequisites: Participants should have working familiarity with oil and gas operations, environmental or sustainability reporting, and basic emissions concepts such as carbon dioxide equivalent, Scope 1, Scope 2, and methane. Prior exposure to ESG reporting, HSE systems, asset management, or energy management is helpful, but not mandatory. No coding is required, although comfort using spreadsheets for emissions calculations, dashboards, and mitigation tracking will improve the hands-on experience. Advanced climate concepts are taught at operational application level, not engineering design level, so you can focus on what can realistically be assessed, planned, and reported within a 5-day program.
